editorial:
Imagine a world where you stop aging at 25, but every second after that has to be earned. That's the wild setup of In Time, a sci-fi thriller that turns time itself into money. Justin Timberlake plays Will Salas, a factory worker from the poor side of town who suddenly inherits over a century of time from a wealthy stranger. Suddenly rich in the one thing everyone wants, he heads to the fancy districts where the rich live forever. But the corrupt time keepers, led by a relentless cop named Raymond Leon, are hot on his trail. Amanda Seyfried plays Sylvia Weis, a rich girl who gets pulled into Will's dangerous world. The movie has a cool, stylish vibe with a clever idea at its center. It feels like a chase movie mixed with a heist, and the ticking-clock tension keeps you on edge.

The acting is solid, especially Timberlake proving he can carry an action role, and Seyfried brings charm to her part. The action scenes are fun and the pacing rarely slows down. On the downside, the world-building can feel a bit thin and some plot points are hard to believe. Still, if you enjoy fast sci-fi thrillers with a unique concept, this one delivers. It's great for a weekend movie night. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final act, Will and Sylvia rob time banks and give the stolen time to the poor, crashing the system. Raymond Leon chases them but runs out of time and dies. Will and Sylvia keep robbing banks, becoming modern-day Robin Hoods. The last scene shows them planning another heist, proving the rich can't stop them and the poor finally have a chance to live longer.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves sci-fi thrillers with a clever concept
